description: Independent Newton-gravity-integral oracle for the Rayleigh-wave half-space Newtonian-noise acceleration (PR-8b), compared against ANNA eqs.75-76 (arXiv:2603.15157v4 = Harms 2019). See generate_rayleigh_oracle.py module docstring for the full derivation and extrapolation contract.

provenance.upstream_repository: gragra (this repository) -- independent in-repo derivation from the published closed form (see closed_form_reference below), not copied from an external upstream project

definition.relation: a(H) = 2*pi*G*rho_0*gamma*exp(-kH)*(i*e_x - e_z), with e_x the propagation direction and e_z vertical (gamma = eq.76). This oracle reports a_z (real) and the imaginary coefficient of a_x (i.e. a_x/i, real) separately.

anna_to_gragra_mapping.anna_phase_and_axes: ANNA eq.75 uses z-down coordinates and exp(-i*k*x) with implicit exp(+i*omega*t).
anna_to_gragra_mapping.gragra_phase_and_axes: gragra uses z-up coordinates and exp(i*(k*x-omega*t)).
anna_to_gragra_mapping.normalization_sign: The leading minus changes ANNA's positive z-down surface normalization to gragra's positive z-up normalization.
anna_to_gragra_mapping.oracle_reporting: Saved oracle values preserve the existing ANNA-eq.75 component/phase reporting and are not sign-flipped into gragra production vectors.
anna_to_gragra_mapping.gragra_target: Production comparisons target the separately mapped gragra vector v_gragra, not a reinterpretation of the stored oracle scalars.

definition.z_cut_sensitivity: bulk_az_values and bulk_ax_values store the sensitivity sweep; az_tail_error_estimate and ax_tail_error_estimate are the absolute differences of their final two values. tail_error_estimate is a backward-compatible alias for az_tail_error_estimate.

extrapolation_method: least-squares fit f(x)=c0+c1/x+c2/x^2 over period-aligned x_cut_period_stages, initial guess from the largest-x_cut sample only (no closed-form target used as fit input); c0 is the reported x_cut -> infinity value. Stability re-verified by refitting on the last 6 and last 5 stages. Vertical (z_cut) truncation re-verified separately via z_cut_sensitivity.
